title: A glass of water holds more molecules than the ocean holds glasses
body: A 250 ml glass of water contains about 14 moles of H₂O, and each mole is 6.022 × 10²³ molecules, so that’s around 8 × 10²⁴ molecules. The world’s oceans hold roughly 1.4 billion cubic kilometres of water, or about 5 × 10²¹ glassfuls. That means your glass holds over a thousand times more molecules than there are glasses of water in all the seas. Atoms are so small that chemists count them by the mole, not one by one.

slides.prompt: Your glass holds more molecules than the oceans hold glasses. By how much?
slides.detail: About 8 × 10²⁴ molecules in a 250 ml glass, against roughly 5 × 10²¹ glassfuls of water in all the seas.

slides.heading: Your glass against all the oceans
slides.note: 1 sextillion is 10²¹. The glass wins by more than a thousand to one.

slides.clue: The constant 6.022 × 10²³ per mole is named after this Italian scientist
slides.detail: Named after Amedeo Avogadro (1776–1856), who proposed in 1811 that equal volumes of gas hold equal numbers of molecules.
